title.narrative: More and better jobs created for sustainable livelihood opportunities for youth and women

description.narrative:
The CPO is supporting the Government of Zambia in the areas of sustainable job creation, enhancement of human development through skills development in general and specifically in reducing the skills gaps in the renewable energy and energy efficiency subsectors as well as regional energy integration.
The Government, through the Ministry of Labour and Social Security (MLSS) in 2019, revised all legislation related to individual employment were revised and combined into one labour code, the Employment Code act, No.3 of 2019 which was enacted into law in May 2019. Further, Industrial and Labour relations Act is currently under revision and it is expected to be finalized this year. Thus, the CPO will contribute to the dissemination of the new Employment Code Act, No. 3 of 2019 to the workers and employers and in the provision of technical support to the revision of the industrial and labour relations act as well as in the formulation and setting up of Sector Based Minimum Wages.
The ILO has continued to provide technical assistance to the government of Zambia to revise the National Employment and Labour Market Policy (NELMP) and other pro employment policies and strategies such as the TEVET policy, National Industrial Policy, National Trade policy and Micro, Small, Medium Enterprises (MSME) policy with a focus of employment and empowerment of the youth and women. Employment Policy promotion focuses in the implementation of the NELMP and other pro employment policies through an inclusive, gender sensitive and participatory process with the ultimate aim of realigning public and private investment priorities in to creating more and better jobs. The ILO has also continued to technically support the Ministry of Higher Education (MoHE) to enhance its capacity to provide market relevant skills training for youth. This was evidenced by the financial and technical support provided in the development and launch of the Work Based Learning Framework (WBLF) in October 2020 f
